batch_strategy: Freeze these 32 candidate IDs with their supplied packet predictions. Use matched amount and solvent-response experiments to test endpoint-specific relationships, extend recent failure repair only where it remains unresolved, and test loading-solvent effects in a graph with existing controlled-volume contrasts. Select by expected learning value; quantile widths and CW distance are secondary evidence rather than calibrated uncertainty scores.

choices.reason: m4, 5/1, 50 uL; packet prediction 4.95/18.55 mL. High-amount observation 111bfd60a27716526dc8 finished at 20.88, while the measured 2/1 amount contrast a539b04b0ab3606e7dd3 versus 032d9fbb133dff53e005 finished at 14.38 versus 19.73. Tests whether the completion difference persists at 5/1 after retraining raised the prediction.

m4, 2/1, 100 uL; prediction 4.75/16.05. The 100-uL 1/1 observation 5a0302cc67b1fd69b7cd finished at 19.92, already comparable to the high-amount result. This intermediate amount distinguishes an early saturation or step from smooth interpolation between measured 2/1 endpoints.

m182, 2/1, 150 uL; prediction 5.73/15.79. Completes a fixed-amount curve through pure-EA observation 9948433906d4afa41345, 1/1 observation 8f683baab6101dc15006 and 5/1 observation d760d0420b34df595c0c9, with completions 20.41, 18.88 and 22.94. Tests the predicted intervening contraction.

m123, 5/1, 50 uL; prediction 8.06/13.87. The latest fixed-amount sequence 71eae942541acd0523cb, 1b610fb92b30df5ca03f and 7e327de3d5f5fcab9a7e rejected the large predicted 1/1 peak. This locates subsequent retention growth between the nearly flat early sequence and measured 50/1 row 832eaa9c6b2f7a68f2a5.

m81, 1/1, 50 uL; prediction 4.23/8.89. High-amount 1/1 observation 06c0c99f1cfb752ed34b was short, and the 150-uL 2/1 completion reproduced in bee82d193ec1ce4fde27 and 3233c0996a6126a9c036. This low-amount point tests whether the shorter high-amount completion also appears at 1/1, contrasting with m4 and m28.

m197, pure EA, 50 uL; prediction 4.06/11.24. Pairs with the selected 1/1 point to test the boundary of the broad completion seen in 69be7348f9ab10739164 and 35a1d2abee0780ee1d48. The phenolic aldehyde provides a functional-group comparison to m118 without assuming its exceptional 1/1 label transfers.

m197, 1/1, 50 uL; prediction 4.92/27.19. Measured 100- and 150-uL completions are 25.53 and 25.79 in 69be7348f9ab10739164 and 35a1d2abee0780ee1d48. Together with the selected pure-EA point, tests whether broad completion persists at low amount and where the ratio response develops.

m190, pure EA, 100 uL; prediction 3.74/9.88. Extends measured 1/1 and 2/1 observations 03e8372f11ac433be4fa and b73454f4c6942f4deb70 toward stronger eluent. This brominated phenolic-aldehyde comparison constrains structural transfer from the selected salicylaldehyde boundary experiment; amounts differ across graphs, so it is not an isolated bromine-effect test.

m73, 1/1, 50 uL; prediction 4.54/14.65. Supplies a valid neighboring-condition test beside the invalid endpoint ordering in pure-EA observation 3d5a3094cb10eee37b37 and measured 2/1 row 7150b292e8a20dd06f1c0950ad36. The latter ID is not used as evidence; the measured 2/1 anchor is 7150b292e8a20dd06f1c. High CW distance reinforces the gap but does not establish an error.

m85, 1/1, 100 uL; prediction 5.25/11.16. Fills the early-ratio gap at the same amount as 5/1 observation edfd927c8b6bab1e5062 and 10/1 observation 09f7ce5c473ea7ea5d94. Tests early completion curvature in an ordinary aromatic ester after the ether peak hypothesis failed, rather than assuming that failure transfers to every graph.

m177, pure EA, 50 uL; prediction 0.81/7.35. Tests the unusually early predicted onset at an unmeasured boundary of this nitro diaryl ketone. Measured 2/1 row 5f8a81445707df0eaad0 is only a candidate and is not evidence; the measured neighboring anchor is bd76c7bdcd3681374617 at 100 uL. The selected amount pair separates a shared boundary response from an amount-dependent one.

m177, pure EA, 150 uL; prediction 0.80/7.37. Matches the selected 50-uL point in ratio and 1000-uL DCM loading protocol despite almost invariant predictions. Historical observations b514312eda7950cdcf1c and 4862e2fb71344ce16021 show how irregular the weak-eluent endpoint surface can be; this tests whether the strongest-eluent boundary is simpler.

m19, pure EA, 50 uL; prediction 6.63/15.59. At 1/1, a595d5f1882c39914392 and 97297c71a28a2ccbdeeb confirm earlier onset at greater amount with nearly fixed completion. This boundary point, compared with 100-uL observation f8dff14aa7f68363fa60 at 8.83/18.24, tests whether that amount ordering persists or changes in pure EA.

m45, 2/1, 50 uL; prediction 7.25/11.17. Recent 5/1 observations 5cc67d02b8fad1c648d6 and d7bff2b52f60b5fad4bd differ in onset but have virtually equal completion. Comparing this point with measured 100-uL 2/1 row 22fc04337abf53335eb8 tests where the acid's amount-associated onset difference emerges.

m146, 2/1, 150 uL; prediction 17.21/34.27. Completes the amount series with cf36dbeee8bb51632d84 and 2745c6978a8911fc3dda, whose onsets are 20.07 and 16.29. Tests whether the onset decline continues at high amount while completion remains comparatively stable in a fused basic heteroaromatic.

m216, 2/1, 100 uL; prediction 15.68/32.85. Adds an interior amount anchor beside 07933c8c797c30bb0e8e at 150 uL and a matched-ratio structural comparison to m146. The two fused nitrogen graphs need not share an amount response merely because their predicted retention is similar.

m216, 5/1, 50 uL; prediction 29.04/55.20. Extends the low-amount curve from measured 1/1 row d1e71a8278523e7a10e3 and contrasts with 100-uL 5/1 anchor 33ffc69a253a89f15995. Tests transfer of the onset-versus-amount association into a weaker-eluent regime for this basic graph.

m20, 10/1, 50 uL; prediction 19.96/31.05. Recent 2/1 observations 3b41addf80b8138137db and 65e1a58ab8e4aa2f1eb6 showed earlier onset at greater amount. Paired with the selected high amount and measured 100-uL row 374b71ac526fe1051993, tests whether that association persists farther along the neutral ether-acrylate solvent curve.

m20, 10/1, 150 uL; prediction 19.95/31.09. Completes a three-amount comparison whose candidate predictions barely respond to amount. The labels distinguish onset changes from completion changes and provide a neutral acrylate comparison to the measured basic m19 response.

m82, 20/1, 50 uL; prediction 26.36/60.24. Pairs with the selected 150-uL point around measured 100-uL observation 61090cfdcf019e0891a3. Related beta-ketoesters m94 and m95 show substantial amount-associated onset differences at this ratio, so this tests whether ethyl acetoacetate follows that relationship or is a counterexample.

m82, 20/1, 150 uL; prediction 26.35/60.24. The model gives essentially identical endpoints to the selected low amount. Comparing both with 61090cfdcf019e0891a3 and the m94 amount series ffc70e28db22d1cc1f3f, e3a799d0fa90b649a157 and ffffcd6f3b9393846ab4 tests structural transfer of endpoint-specific loading relationships.

m94, 1/1, 50 uL; prediction 7.45/14.10. Starts an early-ratio amount contrast for the cyclopropyl beta-ketoester. Measured 10/1 rows 7ac90b210e42d27c5a04 and 5b445b457a8b897a2d6c show a clear onset difference across these amounts; the pair tests whether it is already present in stronger eluent.

m94, 1/1, 150 uL; prediction 7.44/14.10. Completes the matched contrast despite nearly identical predictions. Measured high-amount pure-EA row d7457b516ddba0143275 and 5/1 row 8a5443659239e3b52e14 bracket the ratio response, while recent m95 and m81 results warn that beta-ketoester completion responses need not transfer uniformly.

m80, 50/1, 50 uL; prediction 5.26/10.83. Tests whether the short 100-uL completion in 08155ffdcb0d27576050 extends to another amount. This is informative because bromomalonate observation 027bbff1ac308c5dd7a1 is much later under the same ratio, while descriptor counts alone do not explain the contrast.

m80, 50/1, 150 uL; prediction 5.26/10.86. Completes the low/high amount test around 08155ffdcb0d27576050. The pair distinguishes a broadly short weak-eluent response from a localized 100-uL result, an alternative made credible by the failed m184 amount-dip replication.

m9, pure EA, 100 uL, DCM 300-uL loading; prediction 3.89/9.38. Pairs with selected PE loading at identical recorded volume and amount. At 50 uL, df4d1cc1a382562c2b31 finished later under DCM than PE-loaded 48f272583f7a8b863fc2. Tests reproducibility of a solvent-identity relationship without changing loading-solvent volume.

m9, pure EA, 100 uL, PE 300-uL loading; prediction 3.87/9.47. Completes the controlled-volume loading-solvent pair. The predictor scarcely distinguishes the protocols, whereas the measured 50-uL pair differs in both onset and completion; these labels test whether that contrast persists at another amount.

m9, 20/1, 100 uL, DCM loading; prediction 5.95/13.30. Matches measured PE-loaded row 34a9b815565879eeb8c1 in all other recorded conditions. The 150-uL protocol pair f8670511cab05ad7141d and 1e5d53b5d5e0e3d96556 differed in completion, so this tests persistence across amount and complements the selected pure-EA pair.

m131, 5/1, 150 uL; prediction 3.98/14.77. Extends recent matched-amount 1/1 and 2/1 observations a78f7bae6726f8eb382a and cfa75012f38a3f8f45d1, which finished at 11.70 and 12.23. Together with selected m214, tests graph-specific completion growth after the early-ratio comparisons were reasonably predicted.

m214, 5/1, 150 uL; prediction 6.19/11.61. Extends the measured early sequence 072ea9156cf6dd75519a, 06906310911a5a7509dd and fdab71468651c1f40792, whose completions rise only from 7.38 to 8.52. Provides a near-matched non-carbonyl comparison to m131 and a boundary on transferring the broad m4/m182 correction.

m13, 2/1, 150 uL; prediction 9.41/21.57. Completes the amount series from 74ce463c8423fbd22dc4 and 6573d8f84faaf7ce4a78, with completions 22.60 and 17.90. Tests whether the intermediate dip persists at high amount in a multifunctional ester, linking the selected ether-acrylate and beta-ketoester experiments without assuming additive acceptor effects.

m191, 1/1, 50 uL; prediction 4.87/22.00. Extends the low-amount dialdehyde curve toward stronger eluent from 5/1 observation 20711ea4080ba078e890 and contrasts with 100-uL 1/1 row ea9c116dcd66aca4039c, measured at 6.10/17.73. Tests early completion growth in a different aldehyde environment from m118 and the phenolic aldehydes.

hypotheses.content: Early-ratio completion responses remain graph dependent and can change substantially while onset changes little. Broad m4, m182 and m197 intervals coexist with relatively short m81, m214 and m123 responses. A single correction for aromatic compounds would obscure these distinctions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The predictor needs separate structure-condition relationships for onset and completion. Local ratio measurements and structural counterexamples can identify where a completion correction should stop.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected m182 and m197 boundary contrasts reproduce broad completion, and do m131, m214, nitroketone and ester measurements retain distinct early-ratio response shapes?

hypotheses.content: Amount associations depend on graph, solvent regime and endpoint. Larger amounts associate with earlier onset in several measured series, while completion can remain nearly fixed, expand, or become shorter at high amount. The m4 1/1 series also cautions against assuming linear completion growth.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Many candidate predictions barely change across amount. Matched contrasts can teach when amount predicts onset, completion or both, while exposing relationships that fail to transfer between ratios or functional-group environments. These are observational associations, not established causal loading laws.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which onset and completion associations persist at the selected earlier or weaker-eluent ratios in basic heteroaromatics, acrylates, beta-ketoesters, fused aromatics and the multifunctional ester?

hypotheses.content: The broad m118 1/1 interval is localized or variable rather than demonstrably extending to pure EA. Its reproducibility remains unresolved, but the new boundary labels do not support spreading the large completion correction across the whole early-ratio surface.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: An exceptional completion label with ordinary neighboring conditions can produce harmful structural transfer. The batch therefore emphasizes different aldehyde contexts and other unresolved condition relationships rather than another ordinary pure-EA interpolation for m118.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can a future eligible independent 1/1 record reproduce the broad completion, and what recorded or unrecorded variability could distinguish it from neighboring conditions?

hypotheses.content: A restricted loading-solvent relationship is plausible for m9: DCM-loaded observations have earlier onset and later completion than PE-loaded observations at equal 300-uL loading-solvent volume in two measured contexts. Whether this persists at 100 uL is unresolved; the weakened m72 protocol interpretation cannot establish a universal shift.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m9 candidate predictions scarcely distinguish loading-solvent identity. Equal-volume contrasts provide a cleaner test of this recorded variable than the earlier m72 experiment, where solvent identity and loading-solvent volume changed together and replication showed substantial variability.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m9 DCM-versus-PE endpoint difference recur at 100 uL in pure EA and at 20/1, or do the new labels weaken this graph-specific interpretation too?

hypotheses.content: The earlier proposal that the pronounced predicted V2 maxima near 1/1 in m123 and m126 represented large reproducible response features is rejected for the tested conditions. The m123 fixed-amount sequence is nearly flat and slightly increasing; anisole shows only a small 1/1-versus-2/1 difference.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The failed peak prediction shows that large numerical novelty can identify interpolation artifacts. Measuring where subsequent growth actually begins can constrain the corrected response curve without imposing the same correction on unrelated graphs.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: After the nearly flat m123 pure-EA-to-2/1 sequence, does completion grow at 5/1 as currently predicted?

hypotheses.content: The low m184 pure-EA result at 100 uL is weak evidence for a reproducible amount dip. The new same-tuple result aligns much more closely with neighboring amounts, so a stable nonmonotonic loading feature is currently unsupported.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The repeat reduces the value of teaching a sharp amount dip from one row. It also motivates checking unmeasured amount boundaries around other surprising isolated records, such as m80 at 50/1, before interpreting them as general graph behavior.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Would further independent replication support a separate low-response mode, or would it continue to favor ordinary neighboring-amount behavior?

hypotheses.content: The short m80 response at 50/1 and 100 uL may extend across amounts, but a localized midpoint result remains an alternative. Existing observations establish short retention at several ratios, yet do not resolve the unmeasured low- and high-amount 50/1 boundaries.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Malonate-family observations differ strongly despite shared ester functionality. Establishing whether m80 is a consistent counterexample can improve structural transfer and prevent a single short record from determining an unjustified weak-eluent response.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are both selected 50/1 amount boundaries short, or does one reveal a substantial onset or completion expansion?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes strengthen endpoint-specific, conditional reasoning while weakening several apparent anomalies. For m4, the 150-uL 5/1 completion was 20.88 mL, with an acquisition-time underprediction of 8.29 mL; its measured 1/1, 2/1 and 5/1 completions remain broad. The 100-uL 1/1 completion of 19.92 is already comparable to the high-amount result, so I now test response shape rather than assume linear amount growth. The m28 150-uL 1/1 completion of 19.96 supports expansion followed by relatively modest additional growth. The m19 1/1 amount contrast reproduced earlier onset at higher amount, with completions near 25.5 mL; m45 at 5/1 similarly changed onset while completion stayed near 18.4 mL. These results motivate transfer tests across ratios and chemical contexts. The large m123 peak failed decisively: measured completions across pure EA, 1/1 and 2/1 were 8.81, 9.11 and 9.43 mL, versus the then-predicted 21.09 mL at 1/1. Anisole likewise did not show the predicted large excess. The m118 pure-EA completions of 8.48 and 11.77 localize rather than extend its exceptional 1/1 result. Replication changed the protocol and variability interpretation: m72's low-amount DCM tuple returned 7.02/20.79 instead of 3.53/10.60, and its 100-uL PE result was close to the measured DCM result. The proposed stable m72 protocol difference is therefore weakened. The m184 repeat at 7.63/15.03 also weakened the earlier midpoint-dip interpretation. Conversely, m81's short 150-uL 2/1 completion reproduced at 7.97, supporting a targeted low-amount contrast. Historical errors quoted here are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch combines local failure repair with tests of where those repairs should generalize. Matched amount experiments span basic, neutral, acidic and nonpolar graphs because recent labels support different onset and completion associations rather than one loading rule. The m4 and m182 measurements refine remaining local alternatives; m81 supplies a contrasting shorter high-amount response. The m123 extension maps growth after a falsified peak, while the aromatic ester, dialdehyde, phenolic-aldehyde and nitroketone measurements explore early-ratio behavior in distinct structural environments. The m80 pair specifically tests whether an isolated short weak-eluent result extends across amounts, informed by the failed m184 dip replication. Three m9 measurements test loading-solvent identity with loading-solvent volume held fixed, following the weakened and confounded m72 interpretation. The m73 neighboring-condition measurement addresses a region influenced by invalid-order observations without treating those observations as a physical retention finding. Several selected labels may be ordinary; their value is to constrain transfer, response curvature and endpoint-specific amount relationships across eligible rows. The supplied quantiles have many zero V2 lower bounds and some crossed V1 quantiles, so their widths are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. V2 minus V1 remains an elution interval, not uncertainty. This design targets predictive generalization after retraining rather than large elution volumes or improved separation performance, while allowing within-tuple variation and missing variables to remain explanations where recorded relationships do not reproduce.
